name: Midas mHYPER
oneLiner: mHYPER is a Midas NAV-accreting liquid-yield token wrapping Hyperithm market-neutral stablecoin strategies; permissioned mint/redeem, not a fixed $1 peg.
collateral: Hyperithm LLC-managed reference portfolio targeting delta-neutral absolute returns through basis arbitrage, market making and on-chain/off-chain yield strategies. The signed July 17, 2026 terms require delta neutrality and cap gross leverage at 8.0x. Tokenholders hold a qualified subordinated issuer certificate, not ownership of the underlying assets; product-specific Security and Collateral are not applicable.
pegMechanism: NAV-linked Swiss-law ledger-based investment certificate, not a fixed $1 peg. The July 17, 2026 final terms specify USDC settlement, zero standard redemption fee, a one-Business-Day realisation period, a 23:59 CET/CEST cutoff and a gate of 15% of outstanding tokens per settlement day. The base prospectus requires payment within five Business Days after the realisation period, subject to applicable gates and market-disruption deferrals. Instant redemption separately charges 0.5% and can retain up to 50% under the Deferred Price Method; neither route guarantees unconditional immediate whole-position liquidity. An Ethereum instant redemption at block 26137236 on October 7, 2026 returned 9.015541 USDC; this small execution does not establish same-notional funded capacity.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: The exact mHYPER ISIN CH1475894585 signed Final Terms dated July 17, 2026 identify Hyperithm LLC's actively managed reference portfolio and expressly require that it always remain delta-neutral. Basis arbitrage, statistical arbitrage, market making, DeFi yield and derivatives are permitted within an 8.0x gross leverage cap. This exact-product binding delta-neutral mandate resolves the synthetic-delta-neutral classification independently of sibling descriptions. The Swiss-law issuer certificate and notional portfolio do not confer underlying ownership or financial assurance. Current protocol totals do not measure hedge coverage, margin buffer or a complete reserve inventory; classification asserts the mechanism family, not compliance or safety.
